description: The bar chart visually compares the Shapley values of three models—mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (green)—across nine morphosyntactic categories arranged along the horizontal axis: L₄⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, T, R₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺, which likely represent left and right contextual positions relative to a target token, with T denoting the target itself. The vertical axis quantifies the Shapley value on a linear scale from 0 to 80, marked at intervals of 20. Within each category, three adjacent bars represent the respective model contributions, with their heights indicating the magnitude of influence. The most striking feature is the pronounced peak in category T, where chLSTM reaches the maximum value of 80, XLM-R attains approximately 70, and mBERT scores around 50—significantly higher than in any other category. In contrast, all other categories exhibit relatively low Shapley values, mostly under 15, with some near-zero contributions in L₃, R₃, and R₄⁺. A consistent pattern emerges in the L₁ and R₁ comparison: for all three models, R₁ values (mBERT ~10, XLM-R ~12, chLSTM ~10) exceed those of L₁ (mBERT ~14, XLM-R ~15, chLSTM ~15), suggesting greater reliance on right-contextual information. The legend in the top-right corner clearly identifies each model by color, and the bars are not sorted by height but by category position, maintaining a structured comparison across linguistic contexts.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley value for different models across various categories. The horizontal axis represents the categories labeled as L_4^+, L_3, L_2, L_1, T, R_1, R_2, R_3, R_4^+, while the vertical axis represents the 'Shapley value,' measured on a linear scale from 0 to 80 with tick intervals of 20 units. Bars are grouped by category, with each group containing three bars representing different models: mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (green). The tallest bars appear in category T, where mBERT has an approximate value of 50, XLM-R about 70, and chLSTM reaching the maximum value of 80. In other categories such as L_4^+, L_3, L_2, L_1, R_1, R_2, R_3, and R_4^+, the bars are all relatively short, generally below 15. Notably, the values for R_1 consistently exceed those for L_1 across all models, indicating a stronger contribution from the right context. A legend is provided in the top right corner.
